title: Water them too
label: YOUR PLANT GETS WATERED
lead: Hook 1 (The object truth), because the drooping plant is a picture everyone gets on frame 0 and the turn to the friend lands in one breath.

hooks.label: YOUR PLANT GETS WATERED
hooks.say: Your plant droops, so you water it. Your friend goes *quiet*, and you scroll past.

hooks.label: YOU MEAN TO CALL THEM
hooks.say: Their name pops up, you think I should call them, and then you *don't*.

hooks.label: WHO CHECKS ON THEM?
hooks.say: When did you last check on the friend who always checks on *you*?

beats.say: Your plant droops, so you water it. Your friend goes *quiet*, and you scroll past.
beats.scene: A small potted plant on a sunny windowsill table, leaves sagging. The leaves droop further as the line lands.

beats.say: Plants are honest like that, they droop the second they're *thirsty*.
beats.scene: Low close angle on the plant and cracked dry soil, dust in the window light.

beats.say: People don't. They just reply a little slower, and stop asking how you *are*.
beats.scene: A phone flat on a dark table, a chat whose messages get shorter and further apart, typing dots that fade away.

beats.say: And you keep meaning to call them *tomorrow*.
beats.scene: A wall clock spinning through days, the room light swinging between morning blue and night, the plant on the sill wilting more.

beats.say: But a friend is a lot like that plant, a little water brings them *back*.
beats.scene: A watering can tips, water pours, the plant lifts upright and turns green.

beats.say: So call them tonight, even a short call *counts*.
beats.scene: The phone lights up with a calling screen, warm lamp light filling the room.

beats.say: And if someone came to mind just now, send this to *them*.
beats.scene: The revived plant beside the glowing phone at golden hour, a new leaf unfurling.
